title: Standing of the Covered Holding as a Step in a Repriced Premium
content:
> What does the standing of the covered holding do to a repriced premium?
>
> A third adjustment is settled against the premium of a Pass and Trip Protection plan worked out afresh on
> the price the covered holding's record shows, and it turns on how that holding came to stand on the
> household's record under the Season Pass Programme.

**Where the covered holding's record shows it renewed from a previous season.** The standing adjustment is
-4.00 per cent.

**Where the covered holding's record shows it carried forward from a previous season.** The standing
adjustment is -2.50 per cent.

**Where the covered holding's record shows it neither renewed nor carried forward.** There is no standing
adjustment. A holding opened fresh for the season is such a case.

**What the percentage is taken of.** Each of the two percentages above is a percentage of the bounded premium
— the premium at the new value once the plan's smallest and largest premium have been applied to it — and the
bounded premium so adjusted is rounded to the cent. The percentage is taken of the bounded premium itself,
never of the premium frozen on the plan and never of an amount another percentage settled against the same
premium has already moved; where more than one percentage is settled against it, the percentages are added
into one total and the bounded premium is adjusted once by that total.

**And in figures?** On a bounded premium of 160.00 USD, a covered holding renewed from a previous season
carries a step worth 6.40 USD off that premium, and one carried forward from a previous season carries a step
worth 4.00 USD off it. A covered holding whose record shows neither leaves the bounded premium untouched on
this ground.
